Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 3.

ms:

Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 2.

ms:

items.stem:
The equation of a curve is y = x2 − 5x + 7.
P is the point on the curve where x = 4.

parts.t: Find the gradient of the curve at P.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at P. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.

ms:
M1 for P = (4, 3) and substituting into y − 3 = their m(x − 4) oe
A1 cao
sols: the tangent must pass through the point of contact

parts.t: Show that dy⁄dx = 4x + 7.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point of the curve.

ms:
M1 for expanding to 2x2 + 7x − 15
A1 for differentiating to 4x + 7 nfww

M1 for 4x + 7 = 0 leading to x = −1.75 oe
A1 for the y-coordinate −21.125 oe (−169⁄8)
sols: Expand the brackets first — the product rule is not needed.

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Work out the value of x for which y has a stationary value, and find this value of y.

ms:
M1 for 18x−1 seen or −18x−2 seen
A1 for 2 − 18⁄x2 oe

M1 for their derivative = 0 leading to x2 = 9
A1 for x = 3 and y = 12
x = −3 must be rejected since x > 0
sols: Write the fraction as a power: y = 2x + 18x−1
Check: at x = 2.95, y = 12.0017 and at x = 3.05, y = 12.0016, so this is a minimum ✓

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find the coordinates of the two stationary points on the curve.

ms:
M1 for their derivative = 0 leading to x2 = 4
A1 for x = 2 and x = −2
A1 for both y-values, cao
sols: 3x2 from x3, −12 from −12x, and 0 from the constant 2.
a square root gives both a positive and a negative value

items.stem:
The diagram shows an open rectangular tank with a square base of side x metres and height h metres.
The tank has no lid and its volume is 32 m3.
The total surface area of the tank is A m2.

parts.t: Show that A = x2 + 128⁄x.
Find dA⁄dx.
Work out the value of x that makes A a minimum, and find this minimum surface area.

ms:
M1 for their derivative = 0 leading to x3 = 64
A1 for x = 4 and A = 48 m2
sols: the base is a square of side x
The tank is open, so the surface is one square base and four rectangular sides.

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find the coordinates of the two stationary points on the curve.
Determine whether each stationary point is a maximum or a minimum. Give a reason for each answer.

ms:
B2 cao
B1 for two terms correct

M1 for their derivative = 0 solved, e.g. 3(x + 3)(x − 1) = 0
A1 for both points, cao

B1 for each, with a reason
reason may be d2y⁄dx2 = 6x + 6 with 12 > 0 and −12 < 0, or a correct sign test on dy⁄dx either side
FT their (b)
sols: the second derivative tests the nature of a stationary point
the second derivative is positive, so the curve is bending upwards
the second derivative is negative, so the curve is bending downwards

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find d2y⁄dx2.

sols: multiply by the power and reduce the power by 1
Differentiate the answer to part (a) again.
the second derivative is the derivative of the derivative

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 2.

ms:
M1 for 12x−2 seen or −24x−3 seen
A1 for 1 − 24⁄x3 oe
sols: Write the fraction as a power: y = 12x−2 + x
so the rule for axn can be used
multiply by −2, then reduce the power to −3
the curve slopes downwards at this point

parts.t: Find the value of x at the point where the gradient of the curve is 10.

sols: the derivative gives the gradient at any point

items.stem:

The curve crosses the y-axis at the point A.

parts.t: Write down the coordinates of A.
Find the gradient of the curve at A.
Find f′(x).
Find the value of f′(1).

sols: multiply by 5, reduce the power to 4
the fraction and the power cancel
the derivative of a constant is 0

items.stem:
The equation of a curve is y = x2 − 3x + 4.
The tangent to the curve at the point P is parallel to the line y = 5x − 2.

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find the coordinates of P.

ms:
M1 for their derivative = 5
A1 for x = 4
A1 for y = 8
sols: Parallel lines have equal gradients, so the gradient at P is 5.

The gradient of the curve at the point where x = 2 is 15.

parts.t: Find the value of a.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point of the curve.

ms:
M1 for 6x + 3 = 0 oe, FT their a
A1 cao, oe (−1⁄2, −3⁄4)

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Find the range of values of x for which the gradient of the curve is negative.

ms:
B2 cao
B1 for two terms correct

M1 for 3(x − 1)(x − 3) or critical values 1 and 3 seen
A1 cao
sols: The quadratic is zero at x = 1 and x = 3 and is negative between them.
a positive quadratic is below zero between its roots

T is the point on the curve where x = 1.

parts.t:
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at T.
Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
Find the coordinates of the point where this tangent crosses the x-axis.

ms:
M1 for dy⁄dx = 3x2 − 4 and gradient −1
M1 for T = (1, −3) and y + 3 = their m(x − 1) oe
A1 cao
sols: the tangent has the same gradient as the curve at T

The curve has three stationary points.
Find the coordinates of all three.

ms:
M1 for 4x(x2 − 4) = 0 oe
A1 for x = 0, 2, −2
A1 for all three y-values

parts.t: Find dy⁄dx.
Explain why the curve has no stationary points.
Find the two values of x at which the gradient of the curve is 17.

ms:
M1 for stating that a stationary point needs dy⁄dx = 0
A1 for a correct argument that 3x2 + 5 > 0 for all x, e.g. x2 = −5⁄3 has no solution
sols: A stationary point would need dy⁄dx = 0, i.e. 3x2 + 5 = 0.
the gradient is zero at a stationary point
3x2 + 5 ≥ 5 for every x, so the gradient is never zero and there are no stationary points.

items.stem:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards.
Its height, h metres, above the ground t seconds after it is thrown is given by
h = 20t − 5t2.

parts.t: Find dh⁄dt.
Find the rate at which the height is increasing when t = 1.
Find the maximum height reached by the ball.

sols: The rate of change of height is dh⁄dt.
the derivative measures how fast h is changing
At the maximum height the rate of change is zero: 20 − 10t = 0
the ball reaches its highest point after 2 seconds
Check: at t = 1.9, h = 19.95 and at t = 2.1, h = 19.95, both lower ✓

items.stem:
A farmer uses 60 m of fencing to make a rectangular pen against a straight wall.
The wall forms one side of the pen, so only three sides need fencing.
The two sides perpendicular to the wall are each x metres long and the side parallel to the wall is y metres long.
The area of the pen is A m2.

parts.t: Show that A = 60x − 2x2.
Find dA⁄dx.
Find the value of x that gives the largest possible area, and find this area.

ms: B1 for y = 60 − 2x and A = xy leading to the result nfww
sols: the wall side needs no fence
the maximum is a stationary point
Check: d2A⁄dx2 = −4 < 0, so this is a maximum ✓
the pen is 15 m by 30 m

items.stem:
A square of side x cm is cut from each corner of a square sheet of card of side 30 cm.
The card is then folded along the dashed lines to make an open box of volume V cm3.

parts.t: Show that V = 4x3 − 120x2 + 900x.
Find dV⁄dx.
Find the value of x that gives the maximum volume, and find this maximum volume.

ms:
M1 for V = x(30 − 2x)2 or x(30 − 2x)(30 − 2x)
A1 for correct expansion to the given form nfww

M1 for their derivative = 0 and solving, e.g. 12(x − 5)(x − 15) = 0
A1 for x = 5 (15 rejected)
A1 for 2000 cm3
sols: The base of the box is a square of side 30 − 2x and its height is x.
x is removed from both ends of each edge
x = 15 gives a base of side 0, so x = 5
x must be less than 15 for a box to exist
base 20 cm by 20 cm, height 5 cm

items.stem:
The equation of a curve is y = x3 + ax2 + bx + 4, where a and b are constants.
The curve has a stationary point at (1, 3).

parts.t: Find the value of a and the value of b.
Find the x-coordinate of the other stationary point of the curve.

ms:
M1 for substituting (1, 3): 1 + a + b + 4 = 3
M1 for dy⁄dx = 3x2 + 2ax + b and 3 + 2a + b = 0
A1 for a = −1
A1 for b = −1

M1 for 3x2 − 2x − 1 = 0 factorised or solved, FT their a, b
A1 oe −0.333
sols: The point (1, 3) is on the curve: 1 + a + b + 4 = 3, so a + b = −2.
The gradient is zero at x = 1: 3 + 2a + b = 0, so 2a + b = −3.
one factor must be (x − 1) since x = 1 is a root
